PROVED: 
ORDER OF THE COMMISSION 
Ind. Code ch. 8-1-26 provides the procedure for the Indiana  Utility Regulatory 
Commission’s Pipeline Safety Division (“Division”) to find violations  of said  chapter. Upon 
review of those findings,  the Indiana Underground Plant Protection Advisory Committee 
(“Advisory Committee”) reviews those recommendations and recommends civil penalties in the 
Case.   
The Cases received pursuant to Ind. Code ch. 8-1-26 and ripe for Commission action are 
attached hereto and collectively referred to as the Advisory Committee Recommendations.  
Pursuant to statute, the Advisory Committee has submitted their recommendations  to the 
Commission. The Commission UPHOLDS the findings  of violations  by the Pipeline  Safety 
Division and APPROVES the recommendations  of the Advisory  Committee as listed on the 
attached pages. The Assistant General Counsel to the Division is directed to prepare and send 
notice to the parties advising them of the determination. 
Any approved civil penalties are due within 90 days of the date of this Order unless 
payment arrangements are made with the Secretary of the Commission.   
Any approved trainings must be completed no later than 180 days from the date of this 
Order or the alternative civil penalty noted in the attached recommendation is due.   
IT IS SO ORDERED. 
HUSTON, KREVDA, AND OBER CONCUR; ZIEGNER AND FREEMAN ABSENT: 
APPROVED: 
I hereby certify that the above is a true 
and correct copy of the Order as ap proved. 
Dana Kosco
Secretary of the Commission

import re,glob,collections
c=collections.Counter();n=0;bad=[]
for f in sorted(glob.glob('*.txt')):
    pages=re.split(r'=== page \d+',open(f).read())[1:]
    for i,p in enumerate(pages,1):
        if 'finds the following' not in p: continue
        seg=p.split('finds the following',1)[1].split('recommends the following')[0]
        seg=seg.split('):',1)[-1].strip()
        if not seg: bad.append((f,i,'blank',re.findall(r'Case Number:\s*(\S*)',p))); continue
        m=re.search(r'IC\s*8-[1lI]-26-\s*(\S+)',seg)
        if not m: bad.append((f,i,seg[:60])); continue
        b=re.sub(r'\([A-Za-z][A-Za-z\-]+\)','',m.group(1))
        c[b]+=1;n+=1
print(n);print(bad)
for k,v in c.most_common(): print(repr(k),v,round(100*v/n,3))
E

Across all five years, **39.5%** of cases have base section 16(h), and **22.9%** have base section 20(a)(2).

I counted from the text of all 58 orders, which hold 9,951 cases. I counted one case per recommendation form page that has a cite.

| Base section | Cases | Share of 9,951 |
|---|---|---|
| 16(h) | 3,935 | 39.54% |
| 20(a)(2) | 2,283 | 22.94% |

- **Qualifiers:** I stripped parenthesized words of two or more letters, such as (expire) and (locator-error), before grouping.
- **Scanning errors:** Some cites came through the scan misread, such as "8-l-26" for "8-1-26" and "20(a)(l)" for "20(a)(1)". I read these as the intended cite. Under that reading, 20(a)(l) is 20(a)(1) and lS(h) is 18(h).
- **Excluded forms:** I left out six pages that are blank recommendation forms with no cite. Five are fully blank; the sixth (case 24409 in the 2/23/22 order) has only a respondent and a training penalty. I also left out the cover page of each order.
- **Included form:** I counted the nunc pro tunc order of 4/6/22, which holds one form, as an order.
